script: It's 3 a.m. and your brain won't shut up. Replaying everything you said, everything you didn't. You're not broken, and you're not the only one awake. That racing feeling isn't a flaw, it's an alarm stuck on high. You can't delete it, but you can learn to turn the volume down. I wrote the book I wish I'd had at 3 a.m. The full toolkit's in my bio.
broll_prompt: Multi-shot cinematic vertical sequence, handheld 24fps with subtle micro-jitter, practical lighting, film grain. SHOT 1 (0-2s): extreme close-up of a phone screen glowing 3:00 AM in a pitch-dark room, harsh blue light on a tense face turned away, anxious sleepless tension. SHOT 2 (2-5s): fast restless POV glimpses, ceiling shadows, a clock, tangled bedsheets, a hand rubbing tired eyes, cold blue darkness. SHOT 3 (5-9s): the camera slowly drifts as the harsh blue light softens into a warm dawn glow seeping through a window, a volume dial slowly turning down, tension easing, transition from cold blue to warm amber. SHOT 4 (9-15s): a calm hand writing in an open notebook by soft morning light, pen pressure on paper, a slow page turn, a quiet relieved exhale, hopeful warm cinematic tone. No faces, no text overlays.
